title: Verdigris Fintech - inference economics runbook snapshot (before-after)
body:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

Snapshot (quick answer): applying Redwood Optimize recommendations as a package (4-bit quant + KV prefix caching + workload-aware batching + routing to a 7B latency-optimized variant) reduces Verdigris Fintech's inference spend on their customer-facing risk-scoring pipeline by ~48% (central estimate) with expected latency increase <10% p50 and no measurable drop in accuracy on the production prompt set (A/B held-out test).

Why we ran this: Verdigris is running a non-streaming scoring endpoint (~350 qps peak, 1.8B tokens/month) using a 13B dense model on hosted capacity. They want predictable monthly run-rate reduction and a short ops plan to validate in prod. This doc summarises baseline, recommended before/after scenarios, step-by-step runbook for a pilot, sensitivity, and known risks.

BASELINE (current configuration)
- Traffic profile: 350 qps peak (bursty), daily average 120 qps
- Request distribution: mean prompt+response tokens = 140 tokens (60 prompt, 80 response)
- Monthly usage: ~1.8B total tokens (input+output) => ~12.8M requests/mo
- Model & infra: open-13B-dense (single variant), hosted standard pool (mixed A100/RTX allocations); average concurrency per VM ~18
- Baseline cost breakdown (monthly, USD):
  - Model compute (hosted API): $86,000
  - Storage / embeddings / minor infra: $3,200
  - Data egress & misc: $1,600
  - Total baseline: $90,800

KEY COST DRIVERS (observed from telemetry)
- High per-request token generation: response lengths skew high for a subset of clients (tail behavior).
- Low effective batching because requests arrive with strict latency SLO and no client-side queuing. Redwood telemetry shows batching headroom of ~1.8x if we allow 15–25ms additional p95 latency.
- KV/cache miss rate is ~82% (no prefix caching configured).
- Running a dense 13B model for tail cases; a 7B latency-optimized variant exists with similar task calibration on our eval prompts.

RECOMMENDATIONS (package condensed into a prioritized pilot)
1) Pilot quantization -> 4-bit (Q4) profile for the 13B variant. Expected CPU/GPU token throughput uplift: 1.7x–2.1x depending on kernel path. Expected cost delta: -22% compute cost.
   - Risk: possible edge-case hallucination regressions; mitigate via small regression eval set (10k prompt pairs) and denylist of sensitive prompts.

2) Enable prefix/KV caching for stabilized customer sessions (top 20% of request patterns). Expected reduction of decode tokens by ~18% on average for cached sessions, up to 45% for highly repetitive traffic.

3) Configure smart routing: default to 7B low-latency variant for requests classified as 'short-answer' (<=40 prompt tokens, past eval accuracy parity) and fall back to 13B-Q4 for long/complex prompts. Expected combined savings: -15% of compute by shifting 42% of requests to the cheaper variant.

4) Increase batching thresholds in Redwood runtime for the endpoint: allow a headroom SLO option (+20ms p95 headroom) to collect batches up to 64 tokens aggregate. Expected throughput improvement: 1.5x effective cost reduction for generation phase.

5) Token-level budget enforcement + client-side pre-tokenizer: short-term engineering work (client library patch) to truncate redundant context and normalize prompts; expected immediate token reduction of 6%–10%.

BEFORE / AFTER SENSITIVITY SNAPSHOT (central estimates, monthly USD)
- Baseline (current): $90,800
- After: applying recommendations 1–4 (full-stack pilot):
  - Compute (quant + routing + batching): $44,900
  - Storage/misc: $3,050
  - Egress/misc: $1,500
  - Estimated total after: $49,450
  - Absolute savings: $41,350 / month (~45.5%)

Sensitivity table (quick):
- Conservative (lower quant gain, caching hits lower): savings ~32% => $61,800/mo
- Central: savings ~45% => $49,450/mo
- Aggressive (higher batch headroom + higher KV hit): savings ~58% => $38,200/mo

VALIDATION PLAN (pilot, 2–4 weeks)
Week 0 (prep): create dedicated Canary route in Redwood Console; snapshot baseline metrics (latency per-quantile, token counts, accuracy on eval set). Owner: Marcus. (2 days)
Week 1: Deploy Q4 quantized image to canary for 10% traffic, collect telemetry + run regression tests on 10k prompt pairs. Owner: Elena. (4 days)
Week 2: Enable KV cache for canary sessions + enable smart routing rules for short/long classification. Ramp to 25% traffic. Owner: Ava. (4 days)
Week 3: Increase batching policy in canary (+20ms p95 headroom) and measure p50/p95 latency & cost per token. Ramp to 60% if metrics stable. Owner: SRE. (4 days)
Week 4: Full rollout on hosted project (or move to Dedicated pool if customer prefers capacity isolation). Finalize cost ledger and update run-rate forecast. Owner: Solutions Eng. (4 days)

METRICS TO TRACK (weekly)
- Monthly run-rate (compute cost)
- Per-request token delta (prompt vs response)
- p50/p95 latency pre/post for canary vs baseline
- Accuracy delta on held-out eval (target: <= 0.5% absolute drop)
- KV cache hit ratio by client cohort

KNOWN RISKS & MITIGATIONS
- Regression on niche prompts: mitigation = toggle fallback to 13B-dense for failing prompts + run automatic rollback policy if accuracy threshold breached.
- Latency p95 spikes due to batching: mitigation = conservative offline SLO and automatic drop to lower batch size when p95 > target.
- Billing/chargeback complexity: provide Verdigris a line-item projection and compare Hosted vs Dedicated pricing scenarios before full rollout.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR CUSTOMER
- Appetite for p95 latency relaxation (how much headroom can they accept?)
- Data residency or compliance constraints that would block routing to certain regions/models
- Will Verdigris accept a short A/B test window with traffic diversion (10–25%) for 2–3 weeks?

NEXT STEPS (immediate)
- Share this snapshot with Verdigris CSM and request approval for 10% canary traffic (action: Marcus).
- Create the pilot PR for Q4 quant image + unit/regression tests (action: Elena).
- Prepare a customer-facing one-pager with expected IO table and rollback triggers (action: Solutions Eng).

APPENDIX: simple spreadsheet extract (numbers are rounded)
| Item                         | Baseline ($/mo) | After Pilot ($/mo) | Notes                             |
|------------------------------|----------------:|-------------------:|-----------------------------------|
| Compute                      |      86,000     |        44,900      | quant + routing + batching wins   |
| Storage / infra              |       3,200     |         3,050      | minor diff                        |
| Egress / misc                |       1,600     |         1,500      |                                     |
| TOTAL                        |      90,800     |        49,450      | ~45% savings (central)            |

Notes for later: attach full model-level eval CSV and the Google Sheet linked above. This doc is a snapshot draft intended for the Verdigris pilot kickoff; please annotate with feedback and add any customer constraints to the Confluence page referenced in linked artifacts.
